note: A column mostly one value with per-row overrides on every 10th row. Factored form declares the default + a sparse exceptions list; rows drop the column. Tests whether models honor overrides AND do not misapply them to default rows.
finding: Exceptions are read correctly (pooled 23/24=96% both forms; weak command-r/mistral-nemo 6/6 in factored). BUT the exceptions list causes weak models to misattribute override values to DEFAULT rows: command-r 100->83, mistral-nemo 83->67, all failures on default rows returning an exception value. Frontier (gemini-3.8-flash, llama-3.3-70b) handles it 100%. So near-constant-with-exceptions is NOT safe-tier; frontier-only/tier-gated. CONTRAST: fully-constant factoring (constant-column-comprehension.json) was 100% safe on these same weak models. The exceptions list is what reintroduces the weak-model hazard.
